title: Wide cross-platform discovery pass 44
summary: Personally inspect 36 roots: add 34 projects, defer one oversized source archive and exclude one false CP/M match.
notes: Root personally ran 52 cross-platform searches yielding 564 hits and 560 distinct repository URLs, inspected 36 selected roots, and prepared 34 additions plus two explicit non-promotions. Search covered classic computers, consoles, handhelds, firmware, language/runtime reconstructions, source recovery, development tools, asset/audio/disk tools and binary analysis. Broad coverage is not exhaustion of every platform. No discovery worker used and no upstream software or game content executed. Current catalogues were refreshed from 48f2cbd2ff2e4dc2bd1fd108162a6be379901e85; activity history is an older cached file, so trusted-main live validation remains required. Ingestion findings: byte-exact builds may include unrecovered assembly (GX Spirit Caller and Sly); completed matching may retain handwritten assembly/toolchain patches and unresolved names (Parasite Eve II); a complete-firmware goal can conflict with explicit far-from-complete status (uOFW). Resolve platform collisions from implementation: Educational System Master Cartridge is Atari, CPM-udis86 is CMake, SVP is SSP160x rather than 68000, and a BBC-derived Lisp can target modern Linux. Treat decompiler names as claims: 68000Decompiler emits assembly listings, FPLAY processes sequence bytecode, Pandemonium publishes semantic notes rather than C. BASIC renumberer splits colons before protecting quoted strings, rewrites ON expressions to a placeholder and can remap targets twice, so blanket preservation claims are not ingested. N64 networking is PC-tethered; WonderSwan checksum generation is not validation; audio format/container support is not decoder equivalence. Missing README did not prevent source-based review. Oversized source returned empty without error, while a large recursive tree failed transport: the latter was recovered through commit-pinned file reads, and the former retained as an explicit inspection backlog rather than silently accepted or classified empty. Preserve AI review/demonstration scope and licence restrictions; no build flags promoted from prose alone.

sources.reason: Interactive historical essay backed by an implemented tokenizer, interpreter and browser environment. Recreates a small BASIC programming experience rather than the complete C64 ROM or cycle-accurate machine.

Integrated SDCC, binary utilities, image creation and C firmware wrappers. Reviewed CRTC helper explicitly excludes 32 KiB overscan and screens above 256 lines; broad toolchain support does not remove per-routine limits.
Creates CDT/TZX images from host files, including block and headerless methods. This continuation adds macOS build compatibility and output changes.

C implementation derived from BBC Micro Lisp with function compilation, persistence and X11 turtle graphics. This is a modern-host descendant, not a BBC-native compiler. README warns that strings are not garbage collected.

Guest daemon and host protocol expose remote Apple Events, files, screenshots and native verbs over TCP or serial. Optional MCP is a frontend rather than a requirement for the bridge. ToolServer returns output, while MPW Shell fallback replies empty.

Implemented ASCII renumbering helper, but source contradicts universal preservation claims: it splits on colons before masking strings, and its ON branch emits literal ON ... instead of the original selector. GOTO rewriting also precedes ON-list rewriting. Not safe as an arbitrary-dialect source transformation.
ROM reconstruction has xa assembly, substantial byte tables and da65 code/data/label configuration. A byte-preserving representation is not equivalent to fully interpreted assembler internals.
ImGui/SDL editor includes screenshot extraction, configurable assembler output, masked sprites, animation and tiled views. Explicit beta with possible missing functionality.
Haskell tool implements iNES/ZIP loading, memory maps, instruction parsing, slices and pseudo-code presentation with a terminal UI. Not a general completed NES-to-C game decompiler.
Coherent collection converts tiles, Echo music/instruments, PCM, VGM and compressed data, and generates/fixes ROM headers. MIDI-to-Echo conversion is explicitly preliminary.
Implements SSP160x instruction assembly and SVP ROM manipulation alongside research hardware designs. Scope is Virtua Racing cartridge coprocessor, not Mega Drive 68000 instruction assembly.

Compares recorded audio signatures and plots differences to help inspect hardware, emulators and modifications. Signal-generation setup and host analysis are separate stages; this is not a source-code decompiler.

Annotated cartridge listing names tape, keyboard, screen, audio and buffer variables with access references and build files. Search matched Master Cartridge but this is Atari educational software, not Sega Master System.

Game routines reconstructed in C retain a 64 KiB address-indexed memory array and GBA rendering adaptations. Explicit serial and interrupt stubs remain; this is not a completed original-Game-Boy matching build or a general CPU interpreter.
Editors and format knowledge for six AKI wrestling games, including costumes, archives and models. Incomplete tooling and documentation, not a full game reconstruction.
Console library, PC browser/relay, master server and examples enable homebrew networking through flashcart USB. Requires a tethered computer; does not add standalone onboard network hardware.

Function maps, naming reviews and rail/movement/enemy studies cover Saturn and two Windows executables. No decompiled C or runnable game is published; provisional names remain and movement notes explicitly identify misnamed enemy code.
Extracts fixed-layout Latin, Japanese and Sega-specific glyph sets with documented code-point mapping and font IDs. Not a full boot ROM reconstruction or a font repacker.

Upstream reports executable, two overlays and 446 packages matching. Preserve listed handwritten/inline assembly, register pins, assembler/linker-layout patches and unresolved semantic naming/types. A matching build is not a clean portable C-only port.

WIP engine reconstruction for NTSC-U SCUS_971.98 with separate engine, scripting and data progress. Build accepts extracted assembly/data alongside recovered C++; matching does not mean full semantic recovery.
Kernel modules and hardware API documentation aim at open vanilla firmware. README explicitly says far from complete, despite the repository description using complete as a project goal.
Resolves module NIDs from XML databases, creates import/export structures and maps hardware registers. Enriches Ghidra analysis rather than performing complete automatic decompilation.

README headline says ROM rebuilt from C, but detailed progress explicitly separates byte-matched code including assembly from readable-C decompilation. Three-region SHA1 claims are not 100% C recovery.

Compares function/data sections in object files with symbol demangling, rebuild/watch integration and reports. Object matching and metadata-complete flags are not an independently verified complete-game or semantic equivalence measure.
Implemented jdis decodes Tom GPU or Jerry DSP binaries with offsets/base-address options. Assemblers, optimizers and hazard generators are possible future uses of its core, not shipped tools.

SDX2 and ADP4 encoding/decoding with Portfolio stereo layout. FFmpeg container handling does not establish identical ADP4 decoding; README documents differing decoder interpretation and raw-input requirements.
Converts MOD music and four-colour tile graphics, plus ROM checksum writing. Rust rewrite is explicitly unfinished; checksum generation performs no real ROM validation and overwrites input.
Studies driver 2.11a and parses music banks into structured sequence listings, with FASM regeneration macros. Address-prefixed diagnostic listings explicitly cannot be recompiled.

GPL cartridge control-flow traversal patches a hardcoded relocation range. CALL payload knowledge must be edited for each game; assumes calls return and clear condition bits, which author says is not always true. Not a safe universal relocator.

Tk/Pillow editor emits low-resolution monochrome BASIC and TIM output. Generated BASIC packs strings and removes its construction statements on first run; this is intentional output behaviour, not ordinary static image data.

Extracts/rebuilds resources, edits text/fonts/graphics and decompiles script bytecode for SCUMM v5-v8 and HE with per-feature limits. Font and video encoding support is not uniform across every version.

Reimplementation derived from disassembled original AGI with C logic execution and SDL2 platform code. Reads PC v2/v3 game data; listed Amiga mouse commands and early sprite quirks are outstanding ideas, not implemented compatibility.

Text-only engine identifies tables by patterns in Spectrum SNA snapshots. Supports a bounded set of later Adventure International games; no graphics, some missing commands and imperfect Kayleth table extraction.

X68 project decodes opcodes/effective addresses and prints mnemonic listings through TRAP15 console services. Name says decompiler, but inspected implementation is a disassembler, not high-level C recovery.

Relevant emulator disassembly archive with three 35 MB listings, not SNES game code. README and tree verified, but source retrieval returned empty content for an oversized file. Preserve a follow-up for bounded listing inspection; this is an access/inspection limit, not evidence that the implementation is absent.
CPM is the CMake package manager here, not the CP/M operating system. Three-file wrapper retrieves general x86 udis86 and has no demonstrated specific retro-platform analysis contribution.
